pages.story_text: Jordan knelt on the jagged cliff. Below him, the Fire Clan village glowed like a bed of angry embers. It had taken years of searching, but he had finally found them.
Act II begins. Jordan must infiltrate the Fire Clan village.
Act III begins at the Village Core.
Act IV begins at the mountain ascent.
Act V begins in the volcanic sanctum.
Act VI alias. Continue to final sanctum.
He narrowed his eyes as the wind kicked up hot ash. The scent of woodsmoke filled the air. To anyone else, it was just a fire, but to Jordan, it was the smell of the night his world ended.
The orange glow in his eyes blurred into a memory of his own home. He saw the red banners of the Fire Clan waving through the sparks. He saw his people scattered and his village turned to gray dust.
A younger Jordan knelt in the ruins of his home. The heat was unbearable, but his heart felt cold. In that moment, surrounded by smoke, he made a silent promise to find the people who did this.

Jordan stood up from the ash. He knew that to get justice, he could not stay a frightened child. He sought out a mysterious hermit living in the frozen peaks—a man who had been exiled from the Fire Clan long ago.

Jordan climbed into the highest mountains, where the air was thin and the wind bit like a cold blade. He had heard stories of a hermit who lived in a cave made of blue ice. This man was once a great warrior of the Fire Clan before he was cast out.

Inside the cave, a man sat by a small, flickering fire. His face was covered in scars, and his eyes were as sharp as flint. "Who are you to wake an old ghost?" the Exile growled, reaching for a heavy wooden staff.

Jordan did not flinch. "My name is Jordan," he said, his voice steady. "The Fire Clan took everything from me. They burned my home and scattered my people into the wind. I have spent years looking for a way to stop them."

The Exile looked at Jordan's hands and saw the fire of revenge in his eyes. "I know the darkness of that clan better than anyone," the Exile whispered. "If you want to defeat them, you must learn to fight like them. Are you ready for years of pain?"
The Exile nodded slowly. "Then we begin," he said. "The Fire Clan has many secrets. Which path do you wish to master so you can survive the journey ahead?"
The Exile stood on a high rock and began to throw small stones at Jordan. At first, Jordan was too slow and felt the sting of every impact. "Your eyes are too slow," the Exile barked.

For years, Jordan practiced with a blindfold tied tight over his eyes. He stopped trying to see the stones and began to feel the air move. His body began to react before his mind even realized the danger.
In his final test, the Exile swung a wooden blade at Jordan’s neck with full force. Jordan did not think; he simply moved, his body a blur of motion. He was now faster than the strike of a cobra.

pages.story_text: Jordan sat beneath a freezing mountain waterfall, the heavy water crashing onto his shoulders. The cold was like thousands of tiny needles. "If you cannot control your breath, you cannot control the battle," the Exile warned.
For years, Jordan spent his nights sitting in total silence, even as the wind howled and the mountain shook. He learned to lock away fear and anger. Nothing could break his concentration.
The Exile lit a circle of fire around Jordan and told him to wait. As the flames roared, Jordan remained as still as stone. His heart beat slow and steady, even in the face of death.

pages.story_text: The Exile led Jordan to a forest of frozen bamboo and told him to strike it with his bare hands. Each hit sent pain through his arms. "To break your enemy, you must first be unbreakable," the Exile said.
For years, Jordan conditioned his body against the harshest elements. He climbed jagged rocks barefoot and carried heavy stones up mountain peaks. His bones became as strong as iron beams.
In the final trial, the Exile struck Jordan with a heavy wooden staff. The wood snapped in two against Jordan’s chest, but he did not move an inch. He was now a living shield.

pages.story_text: The Exile hung hundreds of tiny bells from the ceiling of a dark room. Jordan’s task was to walk across without making a single sound. "If they hear you, you are already dead," the Exile whispered.
For years, Jordan practiced moving through shadows in total silence. He learned to step only when the wind blew and to hide in shadows thinner than a blade. He became a ghost.
The Exile tracked Jordan through a thick forest for an entire night. Even with sharp eyes, he could not find a footprint. Jordan had become one with the darkness.

Jordan snapped back to the present day. He was back on the cliff, the weight of his gear feeling familiar. He looked at his hands—they were strong now. The boy from the ash was gone.
The fires were bright, and guards patrolled every corner. Jordan had to choose his path carefully. One mistake would alert the entire clan. How should he enter?
Jordan stood at the base of the village wall and looked up toward the wooden walkways above the guards.
The air was thinner up here. Jordan moved across clay tiles while soldiers laughed below, unaware a ghost watched from above.
A guard blocked the narrow beam path.
Near a chimney, Jordan spotted a locked sky-box with the Fire Master seal.
Jordan stepped into the main street as torches cast long shadows across the cobbles.

choices.label: Rush the street and get spotted

pages.story_text: In a side alley, Jordan found a dying Fire Clan scout clutching a wound.
A massive iron gate blocked the inner square.

choices.label: Use Oil Flask on detected guards

pages.story_text: The sewer air was thick and hot. Jordan slipped in sludge and heard his gear snap against stone.
A mutated fire-lizard lunged from the water.

choices.label: Steel absorbs damage but bleeding starts

pages.story_text: Near the exit ladder, Jordan found a Dirty Bandage beside a dead scout.
A rusted grate blocked the sewer exit.

choices.label: Force it open the hard way

pages.story_text: Jordan stepped into the village square. The Fire Master flicked a kunai toward Jordan’s heart.
The Master kicked burning ash into Jordan’s face and lunged with a fast blade.
The Master charged with a red-hot heavy strike.
Wounded and furious, the Fire Master vanished in red smoke and fled toward the volcano.
At the mountain base, three paths cut into the darkness.
Jordan stood at the volcano base and faced three path options.
A vertical wall blocked the route to the summit.
Two Fire Clan ninjas dropped from ash-covered trees.
Because Jordan showed mercy earlier, he found the Crow mark and opened a hidden tunnel.
All paths converged at a narrow bridge over flowing lava.
A massive crack split the final ledge. Jordan had one chance to cross.
Deep in the Volcano Core, the Fire Master offered his shattered helm to an ancient spirit of flame.
A spectral fire-serpent coiled around him. His screams became a thunderous laugh as he transformed.
The spirit pulse shattered pillars and ripped through the mountain toward Jordan’s crossing point.
The mountain groaned as the quake struck.
Jordan landed in a hidden cavern with a Healing Spring and an ancient altar.
Jordan entered the sanctum. The Fire Master now towered as swirling white flame and cracked obsidian.
The Master glitched through space, striking from three angles at once.
Jordan steadied his breath in the heat. The Master hissed as both prepared for the next exchange.
Obsidian pillars rose in overlapping patterns to crush Jordan.
Jordan called out the truth of fear and false discipline. The Master’s white light flared.
The Master’s arm became a plasma whip that carved voids in the air.
Obsidian skin flaked from the Master. Human fear showed beneath the fire.
The Master collapsed reality into a white-hot vacuum.
The vacuum broke. The Master, now a withered husk, warned of Wind and Earth waiting ahead.
Jordan struck true. Disciplined chaos surged into him as controlled crimson flame.
The volcano collapsed as Jordan sprinted through breaking tunnels and burst into open air.
On black sand, Jordan summoned a balanced flame above his palm. In the distance, a Wind Dragon and Earth Golem watched in silence. [THE END... FOR NOW]
Jordan was consumed by the mountain before reaching the sanctum. The path ends here.
